<reflection>
After three experiments, the cumulative negative log-likelihood sums show M3 is the best fit, but M20, M9, M10, M5, M14, etc. are still relatively close. The previous experiment (adding product) helped differentiate somewhat, but many mechanisms remain plausible. To further discriminate, we need to probe a new dimension: substrate concentration. We have not yet varied substrate concentration (all runs used S=1.0). Changing substrate concentration will stress mechanisms that involve substrate inhibition (M7), substrate-dependent deactivation (M11, M16), or dimerization effects that depend on substrate binding (M3). A low substrate condition (S=0.1) with moderate catalyst (0.01) and no product will test whether the reaction rate scales linearly with substrate, which is expected for simple mechanisms (M1), but may deviate for mechanisms with substrate inhibition or higher-order substrate interactions.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
Choosing a low substrate concentration (0.1 M) while keeping catalyst at 0.01 M and product at 0 will help discriminate mechanisms that involve multiple substrate molecules or substrate-dependent steps. For example, M7 (substrate inhibition) would show reduced efficiency at high substrate, but at low substrate it may behave similarly to M1. Conversely, dimerization mechanisms (M2, M3) may show different scaling with catalyst at low substrate. This condition avoids extreme regimes and adds a new dimension to the experimental design, increasing overall discrimination power across the entire set of mechanisms.
</hypothesis>
